items.why: Carl's thesis is the punchiest half-minute of the meeting, opened at the top of the thought: 'the biggest thing is just recognizing that we're going to have AI forever' through 'if that's all you use, you're useless, because anyone can use AI.'

items.kicker: BYU VERTICAL CLOUD LAB · GROUP MEETING · AUGUST 19, 2026
items.title: AI in the lab

items.why: Sterling reads the three prompts that structure the whole meeting (screen share). Interior trim removes silent scrolling.

items.title: Exhibit A: @claude runs a sensor test

items.why: Concrete artifact on screen: Tim's @claude comment that picked up the enclosure, ran the Colab test, and posted results. Interior trim removes silent scrolling.
The meeting's signature analogy: complacency vs. competency. Interior trim (26:39-27:15) drops an aside; kept through the mountain-biking landing.
The counterpoint, with the laugh line 'sorry, I bought it for everybody': you cannot choose not to buy this e-bike, so competent-and-fruitful use is the real question.
The Tony Stark framing: Jarvis is a support to Tony Stark, not doing Tony Stark's work.

Writing the paper yourself vs. backtracking through AI output, from 'I know the difference of myself personally' to the rhetorical 'is this right? is this right?'. Interior trim removes a garbled aside.
Audrey: figuring out what is actually grunt work -- months on generative CAD, 'and that's okay, plenty of us enjoy doing CAD.' Carl's 'that was a rant' lands underneath.
The exchange: Carl's 'very good at image analysis, spatial analysis ... it's not there yet' answered by Audrey's 'it doesn't live in the 3D world with us. It's all just code and stuff.'

pieces.cap_last_text: It's all just code and stuff.

items.why: The pair lands the culture question in two voices, entering on Audrey's 'okay, yeah, no, I can see that': 'I'm probably overusing it' / 'and probably under-using it, so we just need to...'
Reconvene levity that explains where the channel clips came from: 'we are about to get YouTube famous.'
Audrey's concrete action item: teach good AI patterns during onboarding; 'we need some kind of tutorial to show people.'

pieces.cap_last_text: and using it to maybe like debug stuff.

items.why: Sterling: 'we could make a reel of us -- this is good, this is bad.' This compilation is that artifact.
The natural close: 'Okay, we'll probably call it good there. Thanks, Audrey, Carl. Thanks, everybody.'
